newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed, market seen listless.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed, market seen listless.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in quiet trade amid a lack of significant economic data on Monday, with the market seen remaining listless in the near term, analysts said.

"It's going to be flat all week," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "The only big numbers coming out are the GDP report (on Friday) and durables on Wednesday. Right now looking at the expectations, it should be pretty much bond friendly."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond traded unchanged at C$115.15 to yield 6.763 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bonds rose 7/32 to yield 6.42 percent. The spread between the two widened to 34 basis points from 32 basis points at Friday's close.
Canada underperformed the U.S. market amid some weakness in the Canadian dollar, which weakened to as low as C$1.3435 (US$0.7443) from its open at C$1.3409 ($0.7458).

"The Canadian dollar has been struggling today and that's sort of been spilling into the debt market. I also heard that some U.S. accounts are unwiding their long Canada positions into the shortened week," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.

Both Canadian and U.S. benchmark bond markets are expected to see lower than average volumes this week because of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday. Key economic data expected this week includes the U.S. durable orders report out on Wednesday and Canada's real gross domestic product report for the third quarter out on Friday.

In new issues, Hudson's Bay Company on Monday set a C$100 million 6.25 percent debenture due 2002 with an offering price of C$99.673 and an offering yield of 6.321 percent, 100 basis points over the Government of Canada 8.5 percent bond due April 1, 2002.
The underwriters had the option of expanding the principal amount of the issue to C$125 million, depending on its reception in the marketplace.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.04 to C$106.47 to yield 6.126 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 3/32 to yield 6.13 percent.
The negative spread between the two fell to almost zero from one at Friday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.81 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.16 percent.
